newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco water system upgrade, bonds proposed.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco water system upgrade, bonds proposed.

text.p: City officials proposed two bond measures for the November ballot on Wednesday as part of a plan to upgrade San Francisco's aging water system at a cost of up to $2.4 billion over 10 years.
The two bond measures, totaling $304 million, will be considered this week by the San Francisco Board of Supervisors Finance Committee.
One measure would, if passed, upgrade the water system to better withstand earthquakes. The other would improve water quality in the city.
Officials with the city's Public Utilities Commission estimated that it could cost up to $2.4 billion to repair the water system. The commission's 10-year plan includes a total of 67 projects.
